title: Breastfeeding support: positioning and common problems
summary: Core positioning/attachment principles, and recognising and responding to common early feeding problems.

blocks.heading: Signs of good attachment
bullets: A wide-open mouth, more areola visible above the baby's top lip than below it, chin touching the breast, and rhythmic sucking and swallowing with no pain beyond the initial latch.
VERIFY current local infant-feeding training (e.g. UNICEF UK Baby Friendly Initiative materials) for the exact teaching points and positions used locally.

blocks.heading: Sore or damaged nipples
bullets: Usually a sign of an attachment problem — reassess positioning and attachment first before considering other causes.
Persistent problems despite reassessment may need specialist infant-feeding support.

blocks.heading: Engorgement
bullets: Breasts feel full, hard, and tender, typically in the first few days as milk 'comes in'.
Frequent, effective feeding or expressing, warmth before a feed, and a cold compress afterwards are commonly advised — VERIFY current local advice.

blocks.heading: Mastitis
bullets: A localised red, tender, hot area of the breast, sometimes with flu-like symptoms or fever.
Continue breastfeeding or expressing from the affected side where tolerated — this helps clear the blockage.
Seek review if there is a fever, she is systemically unwell, or there is no improvement with simple measures within 12–24 hours.
If she appears systemically unwell, consider the Suspected maternal sepsis emergency drill.

blocks.heading: Tongue-tie
bullets: Can contribute to feeding difficulty for some babies.
Refer per local infant-feeding/tongue-tie pathway if suspected, rather than assessing or treating this independently.
